chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from someone whose name he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Isma'il about whom Allah the Exalted said in His Book, 'And mention in the Book Isma'il. Indeed, he was true to his promise,' was captured, and the skin of his face and head was flayed. Then an angel came to him and said, 'Indeed, Allah has sent me to you, so order me to do whatever you wish.' He said, 'I follow the example of al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him).'

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ عَلِيٍّ: Al-Husayn ibn Ali, the third Imam

ai.seo_question: Who is the Isma'il mentioned in the Quran as being true to his promise, and what was his connection to Imam Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* establishes a profound theological link between the martyrdom of Prophet Ismail (peace be upon him) and Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him), portraying Ismail as the primordial archetype of self-sacrifice. By selecting to be 'an example for Husayn,' the narrative suggests that the spiritual reality of Karbala was pre-ordained and known to the Prophets, reinforcing the Shia concept of the unity of the Ahl al-Bayt's suffering across history. This connection elevates the Battle of Karbala from a historical event to a cosmic, pre-eternal reality known to divine messengers.
